sources.title: Rishi Sunak: ministerial service, education and career
sources.findings: Read the government biography: prime minister 25 October 2022–5 July 2024; chancellor 13 February 2020–5 July 2022; chief secretary 24 July 2019–13 February 2020; parliamentary under-secretary 9 January 2018–24 July 2019. Education lists Winchester, Oxford PPE and Stanford MBA as a Fulbright scholar. The profile is a historical ministerial biography, not evidence of a current premiership.

sources.title: Rishi Sunak: current seat and historical government and party offices
sources.findings: Read the current parliamentary career record: Conservative MP from 7 May 2015; three elections in Richmond (Yorks), with that representation ending at dissolution on 30 May 2024; Richmond and Northallerton from the 4 July 2024 election. Conservative leader 24 October 2022–2 November 2024; official opposition leader 5 July–2 November 2024. Party election and prime-ministerial appointment are separate dates. Boundary change is not treated as a party switch or loss of parliamentary career.

sources.title: Rishi Sunak: birth, education and political biography
sources.findings: Read biographical sections stating birth in Southampton on 12 May 1980, Oxford first-class graduation in 2001 and Stanford MBA in 2006. Birth and MBA year are secondary-source facts, corroborated in broad educational outline by official government and university biographies. No original civil record or degree certificate was inspected. Peripheral family finances and unsourced evaluative claims are not reproduced.

sources.title: Alumnus Rishi Sunak becomes UK prime minister
sources.findings: Read Lincoln College’s alumni announcement: matriculation in 1998, first-class PPE graduation in 2001, subsequent Stanford MBA, financial career and 2015 Richmond election. The college’s hopes for his premiership are attributed opinion, not an assessment of accomplished policy outcomes. This is a historical announcement rather than current office evidence.

sources.title: Chancellor’s coronavirus support announcement, 20 March 2020
sources.findings: Read Treasury’s original script published 20 March 2020, explicitly marked as possibly differing from delivery. It announces employer grants for furloughed workers, initially 80% of pay up to £2,500 monthly, backdated to 1 March, initially at least three months. Application infrastructure and first payments were still prospective. The profile does not claim the script proves every spoken word, immediate disbursement, universal eligibility irrespective of scheme rules, or a measured total of jobs saved.

sources.title: Northern Ireland Protocol: the Windsor Framework
sources.findings: Read Commons Library briefing: political agreement announced by Sunak and von der Leyen on 27 February 2023; trade, VAT, regulation and Stormont Brake arrangements required subsequent procedures. The briefing still describes the 24 March Joint Committee meeting prospectively; it is not used as proof that meeting occurred. The separate European Commission chronology could not be fetched; EUR-Lex extraction returned no substantive text. Accordingly, no exact later adoption or implementation date is asserted.

sources.title: AAA and others: Rwanda policy judgment press summary, 15 November 2023
sources.findings: Read Supreme Court’s own press-summary PDF for the 15 November 2023 AAA judgment. The unanimous decision upholds unlawfulness because of real refoulement and ill-treatment risks under the evidence and arrangements then examined. The MEDP memorandum predated Sunak’s premiership, dating to April 2022. This is judicial review of a policy, not his personal criminal conviction. The full judgment and later Rwanda legislation were not exhaustively reviewed; no assertion that the 2023 ruling alone resolves all later measures is made.

sources.title: Register of Members’ Financial Interests: Rishi Sunak
sources.findings: Read current members’ interests entries: senior advisor to both Anthropic and Microsoft from 9 October 2025, registered 29 October. The Anthropic remuneration agreement has a different September date, which is not substituted for the role start. Registration confirms disclosed outside work; approval advice alone would not prove commencement. Private/contact addresses, pay calculations and speculative conflicts are not included. Other recorded roles and all payments are not exhaustively audited.

sources.title: Business of the House: Sunak’s Northallerton station question, 12 November 2026
sources.findings: Read actual Hansard exchange of 12 November 2026, Sunak’s question and Alan Campbell’s reply: Northallerton station parking, a meeting he said he convened with council, mayor’s office and TransPennine Express, and clarification of the local transport grant. Campbell acknowledged letters to departments and offered follow-up. This supplies recent actual parliamentary activity, not merely a future agenda. Neither speaker establishes final funding approval or completed construction.

sources.publisher: Blavatnik School of Government, University of Oxford
sources.title: Rishi Sunak: financial career and public service
sources.findings: Read Blavatnik biography identifying prior Goldman Sachs and The Children’s Investment Fund employment and co-founding an investment firm, with current Richmond and Northallerton representation. Employment dates, exact co-founder ownership shares and a professorial appointment are not inferred. The university affiliation does not itself confer a new academic degree.

No assumption is made that the general statement overrides a photo-specific exception or that the edited file is publishable under ND terms.
